newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Highlands says don't sell yet.
newsitem.headline: Highlands says don't sell yet.

text.p: Highlands Gold Ltd said on Thursday that it plans to make a comment later today on the takeover offer from Placer Dome Inc, but at the moment it advises shareholders not to sell their shares.
"At the moment, the advice would be not to sell," Highlands company secretary Phillip West told Reuters.
"But the directors are considering the offer and are expected to make a statement later today," West said.
Placer Dome, which has amassed a one third stake in Highlands over the past 24 hours, earlier launched a 75 cents a share bid for the Papua New Guinea miner.
Placer Dome's bid values Highlands at about A$425 million.
The Canadian gold miner also made an offer to mop up the 24.6 percent of its Australian offshoot Placer Pacific Ltd that it did not already own.
Nobody was available to comment at Placer Pacific.
If Placer Dome suceeds in its bids it would control 50 percent of the Porgera gold mine in Papua New Guinea, in which both Highlands and Placer Pacific have a 25 percent stake.
Placer Dome is offering one of its shares for every 15 Placer Pacific. The bids have a total value of US$600 million.
At 10.15 a.m. (2310 GMT), Placer Pacific shares were steady with Wednesday's close of A$1.43, while Highlands was bid at 80 cents, compared with Wednesday's close of 58 cents.
